issues.t: CVT whine or hum that ends in transmission failure
issues.sym: A humming, whining or grinding noise that rises with speed and gets worse over months, often with no warning light. Some cars lose power or coast to a stop when the transmission finally fails, commonly between about 70,000 and 125,000 miles.
issues.why: A bearing inside the continuously variable transmission (CVT) wears out. Toyota does not sell the bearing as a separate repair part, so dealers replace the whole transmission.
issues.next: If you hear a new hum that changes with speed, have it diagnosed before it fails on the road. Ask a Toyota dealer whether any goodwill or extended coverage applies, and get quotes on a remanufactured or used transmission.

issues.t: Windshield chips and cracks easily
issues.sym: Small stones leave chips that quickly turn into long cracks, and some owners need more than one windshield in the first few years.
issues.why: The steeply raked windshield is the most-reported complaint on the 2018 C-HR. Owners report it chipping and cracking from minor road debris.
issues.next: Repair chips right away before they spread. Check your insurance glass coverage, and make sure the front camera is recalibrated after a replacement.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air on and off
issues.sym: With the A/C on, the vents sometimes blow warm air for a while before cooling again.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for intermittent warm air from the vents on these years, with a set repair procedure.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check the A/C and ask about the warm-air bulletin, since the fix may be covered.

issues.t: Water on the floor from a blocked A/C drain
issues.sym: Water on the front passenger floor, a sloshing sound behind the dash, or fogging windows, usually after using the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C drain tube can clog, sometimes with an insect nest, so condensation backs up into the cabin instead of dripping under the car. Toyota has several bulletins on it.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain cleared and dry any wet carpet quickly to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Musty smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A musty or sour smell from the vents, mostly when the A/C first turns on.
issues.why: Moisture and bacteria build up on the A/C evaporator. Toyota published an odor service using a foam cleaner for these years.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and ask a dealer or shop for the evaporator cleaning service. Running the fan without A/C for a few minutes before parking helps.

issues.t: Blower fan keeps running after the car is off
issues.sym: The heater or A/C fan keeps running after you turn the car off, which can drain the battery.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for the blower motor continuing to run when the fan switch was left on at shutdown.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check the blower circuit and apply the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Dead or weak 12-volt battery
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting, the dash lights dim, or you need jump starts, sometimes on a fairly new car.
issues.why: The 12-volt battery can be drained by modules that stay awake after shutdown or simply wear out early. Owners report early battery failures on the C-HR.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. If it keeps dying, ask a dealer to check for parasitic drain and any software updates.

issues.t: Battery drain from accessory fog lights
issues.sym: A low battery, slow cranking or no start, on cars fitted with the dealer-installed fog lights.
issues.why: The accessory fog lamp kit can draw power while the car is parked. Toyota issued a tech tip on the drain.
issues.next: If your car has accessory fog lights and the battery keeps dying, ask a Toyota dealer to check the fog lamp wiring for the known drain.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake may not engage or release (recall)
issues.sym: The electronic parking brake does not set or will not release, and a warning light may come on.
issues.why: A software problem in the brake computer can stop the electronic parking brake from working, so the car could roll if it is not in Park.
issues.next: Always shift into Park before leaving the car. Have a Toyota dealer confirm recall 17V-717 was done; the update is free.

issues.t: Parking brake briefly applies when downshifting (service campaign)
issues.sym: The electronic parking brake may grab for a moment when you use the manual downshift mode.
issues.why: Toyota ran a limited service campaign for brief parking brake activation in certain downshift situations on early cars, and fitted a parking brake switch cover.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether your car received the campaign update. Avoid using the manual downshift mode until confirmed.

issues.t: Parking brake warning or "See Dealer" message
issues.sym: The parking brake or brake warning light comes on by itself, sometimes over bumps, and cruise control may switch off.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the electronic parking brake system on higher-mileage cars, including some that already had the recall done.
issues.next: Have the brake system codes read. Ask a dealer whether the fault is related to the parking brake recall or a failing switch or motor.

issues.t: Brake pedal or steering vibration after tire service
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes when braking, often soon after the wheels were removed for tires or brakes.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin noting that uneven or wrong lug nut tightening can distort the brake rotors and cause vibration.
issues.next: Have the lug nuts tightened with a torque wrench to Toyota's spec. If the vibration stays, the rotors may need resurfacing.

issues.t: Rear wheel hub bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or noise from a rear wheel, or damage to the rear brakes. In the worst case a rear wheel could come off.
issues.why: The bolts holding the rear axle hub were not tightened enough at the factory and can work loose.
issues.next: Get recall 18V-710 done right away if it is open. The dealer replaces the hub and related parts for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may not lock properly (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no symptom. The rear seat belt may not lock as it should, especially in a crash with more than one impact.
issues.why: The locking part of some rear seat belts may not work as designed.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check recall 19V-877. The seat belt is replaced for free.

issues.t: Pre-collision braking may not work (recall)
issues.sym: A pre-collision system warning may show, or forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking may simply not work.
issues.why: The front radar sensor may not have been activated at the factory, leaving the pre-collision system turned off.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check recall 22V-107. The radar sensor is set up for free.

issues.t: Humming wheel bearing
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and changes when you turn or change lanes.
issues.why: Worn wheel bearings are among the problems C-HR owners report.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked. Replace it before the noise gets loud, since a loose bearing can affect handling.

issues.t: Tire pressure light from a failing sensor
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on or flashes even when the tires are inflated correctly.
issues.why: One of the tire pressure sensors in the wheels has failed or its battery has run down.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures. If they are fine, have the sensors tested and replace the bad one.

issues.t: Infotainment freezes or Bluetooth drops
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes or reboots, phones disconnect or will not pair, and audio cuts out.
issues.why: Software problems in the head unit cause most of these complaints. Toyota has issued software updates and Bluetooth pairing tips.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether a head unit software update is available. Deleting and re-pairing the phone fixes many Bluetooth problems.

issues.t: Tire roar above 45 mph
issues.sym: A loud roar or hum from the tires above about 45 mph, often on cars with under 10,000 miles.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin about abnormal noise from the original Dunlop 18-inch tires and some wheel and tire combinations.
issues.next: Have the tires checked and rotated. Ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin if your car still has its original tires.

issues.t: Squeaking rear door handles
issues.sym: A squeak from the hidden rear door handles when you pull them.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for squeaking rear outside door handles on early C-HRs.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply the bulletin repair. It is a comfort issue, not a safety problem.

issues.t: Blurry logo from the mirror puddle lights
issues.sym: The C-HR logo the side mirrors project onto the ground looks blurry or distorted.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin and repair procedure for distorted images from the mirror foot lights.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to replace the puddle light lens under the bulletin if it bothers you.

issues.t: Fuel range estimate not accurate
issues.sym: The miles-to-empty reading drops faster or slower than expected, so you cannot trust how far you can go.
issues.why: Owners report the range readout not matching real fuel use. The estimate is based on recent driving, so it swings a lot.
issues.next: Use the trip meter and fuel gauge together. If the gauge itself is wrong, have the fuel level sender checked.
